newsitem.title: UK: Britain's PIA fines Lincoln for pension failings.
newsitem.headline: Britain's PIA fines Lincoln for pension failings.

text.p: Pension industry watchdog the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) on Tuesday handed out its largest fine to an independent financial adviser (IFA) as part of efforts to clear up Britain's four billion pound ($6.7 billion) pension misselling scandal.
Lincoln Independent Ltd, acquired by Lincoln Group in April 1995, was reprimanded and fined 75,000 pounds by the PIA for failures in the conduct of its pension misselling review.
Lincoln admitted failing to carry out the review in accordance with the standards established by the PIA and compliance with the PIA's principles and rules.
The firm has also agreed to pay PIA costs of 10,000 pounds.
Over 30 IFAs have been fined in connection with the review, most of which have related to failure to submit information rather than the conduct of the review.
The review into the pension misselling scandal was launched by Britain's top financial regulator the Securities and Investments Board in 1994.

As many as 1-1/2 million people may have been wrongly advised by the financial services industry to take out personal pensions in the late 1980s and early 1990s instead of staying in occupational schemes. ($ = 0.594 British Pounds)
